target_customer: Hyperscalers and neoclouds building large AI training and inference clusters
problem: Electrical packet switching inside AI data centers wastes power, adds latency and heat; optical circuit switching keeps traffic in light but needs fast, reliable switches and control software.
business_model: Hardware sales of optical circuit switches plus an AI control layer; seeking design partners and foundry collaborations
product_category: Optical circuit switching hardware for AI clusters

founders.name: Deepankur Thureja
education: ETH Zurich, PhD, ETH Medal for thesis
founders.background_notes: Built quantum optical hardware at ETH Zurich with Nature publications, per the YC page.

founders.name: Gabriele Pasquale
founders.background_notes: Nature Materials publication on a condensed matter problem, per the YC page. Degree level not stated on the page.

competitors.name: nEye
competitors.what: On chip optical circuit switching using silicon photonics and MEMS
competitors.funding_then: $80M Series C in April 2026, about $152M total per one report

competitors.name: Salience Labs
competitors.what: All optical silicon photonic switch, 32 port demo, Tower Semiconductor manufacturing
competitors.funding_then: $30M Series A earlier; a later raise reported at $125M, unverified

competitors.name: Google (Jupiter OCS)
competitors.what: In house optical circuit switching in production data center networks

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires novel photonic switch hardware, foundry fabrication and reliability at data center scale. Coverage notes the founders' papers do not yet prove a shippable product.

defensibility.rationale: Deep physics expertise and possible patents would be hard to copy, but several well funded competitors are ahead on fabrication partners.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against Dipole found as of 2026-11; PsiQuantum also announced switching in October 2026.

market_need_then: AI cluster growth pushes network power and latency limits and investors funded optical switching heavily in 2026; the company claims its switches give a 10,000 GPU cluster the effective performance of 12,500 GPUs, unverified.

branding.domain_note: dipolelabs.com redirects (302) to dipole.com as of 2026-11; the owner history of dipole.com is not documented. Other firms named Dipole exist.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and forward looking: Scaling intelligence with light

brand_strength.rationale: A physics term fitting a photonics company and a short domain, but several unrelated Dipole companies dilute search and no brand press exists.

outcome_analysis: Dipole Labs is a 2026 spinout from Harvard postdocs with strong academic credentials and a timely market, but no verified funding and no shipped product. It enters a field where nEye, Salience Labs and iPronics have raised far more. Its prospects depend on proving a reliable switch and securing foundry and design partner commitments.
notes: Funding: a Dealroom listing seen in a snippet shows $125k seed and Cisco Investments lists Dipole Labs in its portfolio, both unverified and not recorded as rounds. Location conflict: YC page says Boston, website lists San Francisco and Lausanne. Competitor figures come from search summaries of trade press not fully opened. Roles CEO and CTO from the YC page.
